A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Autonomous Imagination work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original counting, jigsaw, object-placement, and ROPE evaluations in Tables 1–2, alongside additional experiments and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds CLEVR, Where2Place, smaller-model, RoboPoint, and o3 evaluations in Tables 3–6.

M1.justification: The closed-loop procedure, cursor control, focus/ignore/transform operators, and conditional segmentation algorithm remain unchanged. The prompts in Figures 15–16 are also identical; the new Section 3.8 reorganizes their explanation.

E1.justification: v4 adds CLEVR geometric-object counting and Where2Place placement in real homes and offices (Section 4.7, Table 3). These substantially broaden the evaluated scene distributions while retaining the original four task families and datasets.

E2.justification: v4 adds RoboPoint, labeled RobotPoint in Table 5, and unenhanced Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL2.5 controls in Table 4. Table 6 adds o3 and its tool-disabled variant alongside o1. Existing main-table and appendix comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Existing protocols remain unchanged. Added evaluations introduce 178 CLEVR test images sampled to balance object counts, Where2Place's 100 scenes, four smaller-model configurations spanning 7B–32B parameters, and an o3 control explicitly prompted to disable tools. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Section 4.7 adds smaller-model applicability tests and analysis of premature stopping and puzzle-completion errors, plus the o3 tool-use ablation in Table 6. Existing difficulty/budget analyses, cursor-only ablations, failure examples, and SmartEdit/CogCoM appendix analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report counting-error means and variances without seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new tables extend the same reporting practice to additional results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the CogCoM table, renumbered from 3 to 7, retain identical values. New Tables 3–6 substantially expand results: CLEVR success is 74.7% with the method versus GPT-4o's 57.3%; Where2Place accuracy is 37.0% versus 29.1%, while RobotPoint achieves 46.8%. Smaller-model and o3 findings are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same probability definitions and factorization, with unchanged conditional-dependence reasoning and segmentation mathematics. No new formal assumptions, propositions, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claim that training-free, closed-loop visual modification decomposes the visual-to-textual bottleneck and enables otherwise difficult visual reasoning. The additional experiments support and qualify this retained contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations concerning smaller-model capabilities, in-domain training versus cross-task reasoning, and multimodal tool use. Sections 4.7 and 5 also identify stopping failures, difficulties measuring scene complexity, and fixed-plan inefficiency, substantially expanding the earlier limitations.

D1.justification: Where v2 only identifies a project page, v4 explicitly reports code and data release there and directs readers to released code for segmentation details. This adds access information; the existing prompts, hardware timing, and API-call disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 2.2 and 4.7 substantially expand positioning against image-editing and concurrent multimodal reasoning research, including o3, GOT, ReFocus, and visual test-time scaling. v4 explicitly distinguishes its visual-to-textual framing from these approaches and adds references supporting the new benchmarks and models.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain intact. v4 adds discussion subsections and a broader-impact appendix, moves the system-prompt overview from Appendix C to Section 3.8, and makes limited wording and front-matter edits.

P2.justification: New Tables 3–6 substantially expand the presentation of benchmark, backbone, in-domain, and tool-use comparisons. Existing figures are retained, but Figure 1 moves before the introduction and Figure 3 adopts a wrapped layout beside the text; the appendix table is renumbered.

improvement.justification: Tables 3–6 substantially strengthen v2's GPT-4o-centered proof of concept through external benchmarks, smaller-backbone tests, and contemporary comparator controls. They establish applicability boundaries, including stopping failures and RobotPoint's Where2Place advantage, while expanded limitations better qualify the contribution. These improve empirical credibility substantially, although repeated-run uncertainty and large general-purpose validation remain absent.
